title: Towards Model-based Run-time Cybersecurity: On Control-Flow Anomaly Detection, Attack Identification, and Hardware Monitoring
abstract: arXiv:2608.11802v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Methods to increase the resilience of systems to cyber-attacks become increasingly important. Control-flow monitoring provides a principled basis to ensure integrity and detect possible anomalies at run-time. Once anomalies have been detected, so-called attack trees can be used to identify possible types of attacks. However, this approach is vulnerable to camouflage, by which attackers try to evade detection (and correct identification) by deliberately manipulating also the system's observed control flow. In this paper, we outline a model-based approach that provides more robust intrusion detection and attack identification through an architecture that combines software- with hardware-based monitoring. In this approach, software-level observation indicates suspicious activities, while hardware-level monitoring checks them separately in more detail, making it much harder for attacks to camouflage themselves and go undetected. translated_title: 面向模型驱动的运行时网络安全：控制流异常检测、攻击识别与硬件监控
translated_abstract: 提高系统对网络攻击的韧性方法变得越来越重要。控制流监控为确保系统完整性并在运行时检测潜在异常提供了原则性基础。一旦检测到异常，所谓的攻击树可用于识别可能的攻击类型。然而，这种方法容易受到伪装攻击的影响，攻击者通过故意操纵系统观察到的控制流来试图逃避检测（和正确识别）。本文概述了一种基于模型的方法，通过结合软件和硬件监控的架构，提供更稳健的入侵检测和攻击识别。在该方法中，软件级观察指示可疑活动，而硬件级监控则独立且更详细地检查这些活动，使得攻击更难伪装自身并避免被检测。我们通过示例说明了这一方法。
tldr: 本文提出一种结合软件与硬件监控的模型驱动方法，通过双重检查机制增强控制流异常检测和攻击识别，有效抵御伪装攻击。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a model-driven approach combining software and hardware monitoring to enhance control-flow anomaly detection and attack identification, effectively resisting camouflage attacks.
